reason: The sources provide over 20 well-supported, dramatic claims detailing the exact timeline, eyewitness actions, and historical aftermath of Gandhi's assassination.
story: On January 30, 1948, Mahatma Gandhi walked out to his evening prayer meeting at Birla House in New Delhi. At 78 years old, and having survived a bombing just ten days prior, he refused armed protection, leaning instead on his young grandnieces, whom he called his "walking sticks." Suddenly, Nathuram Godse, a Hindu nationalist from Pune, stepped out of the crowd. Godse bowed in reverence, then drew a Beretta pistol and fired three point-blank shots into Gandhi's chest and stomach. As Gandhi fell, gasping "He Ram," the crowd stood paralyzed. It was a newly arrived American vice-consul, Herbert Reiner Jr., who broke the spell by tackling Godse. A Royal Indian Air Force sergeant wrenched the gun away, and police saved Godse from a lynching. Carried inside, Gandhi died shortly after. That night, Prime Minister Nehru announced to a grieving nation, "The light has gone out of our lives."
angle: As the crowd stood paralyzed in shock after Mahatma Gandhi was shot, it was a newly arrived 32-year-old American vice-consul who broke the spell by lunging forward and tackling the armed assassin.

claims.claim: Mahatma Gandhi was assassinated on January 30, 1948, in the gardens of Birla House in New Delhi.
Gandhi was 78 years old at the time of his death.
The assassin was Nathuram Godse, a Hindu nationalist originally from Pune.
Godse fired three bullets at point-blank range into Gandhi's chest and stomach.
The shooting took place as Gandhi was walking to his daily evening prayer meeting.
During the walk, Gandhi was leaning on the shoulders of his grandnieces, whom he referred to as his walking sticks.
As he fell to the ground, Gandhi uttered his final words, 'He Ram' ('Oh God').
The shooting occurred at approximately 5:15 p.m. or 5:17 p.m.
While the crowd was paralyzed with shock, newly arrived American vice-consul Herbert Reiner Jr. seized the assassin by the shoulders.
A Royal Indian Air Force flight sergeant wrenched the Beretta pistol away from the assassin.
Ten days prior to the assassination, conspirators had made an unsuccessful bomb or grenade attack against Gandhi at Birla House.
Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru announced Gandhi's death over the radio, stating that the light had gone out of their lives.
Godse was an editor and journalist associated with the right-wing Hindu Mahasabha and the RSS.
Immediately after the shooting, an angry crowd fell upon and beat Godse before police took custody of him.
Following his arrest, Godse told reporters that he was not sorry for what he had done.
Godse and his co-conspirator Narayan Apte were sentenced to death and hanged on November 15, 1949, at Ambala prison.
Gandhi had survived an earlier assassination attempt on June 25, 1934, in Pune when a bomb was thrown.
The news of the assassination sparked violent riots in Bombay, leaving fifteen people dead.
After being shot, Gandhi was carried back into Birla House, where he died shortly after.

disputed: Whether Gandhi died instantly or 30 minutes later: S2 states he was dead within seconds at 5:17 p.m., while S1, S3, and S4 state he died about 30 minutes later after being carried inside. A script should state that accounts differ on whether he died instantly or within thirty minutes.

Whether Godse fired a fourth shot: S4 reports Godse fired a fourth shot to kill himself, but was stopped, while S3 reports his pistol still had four undischarged cartridges when snatched. A script should leave out the detail of a fourth shot.

Whether Godse surrendered voluntarily or was tackled: S1 notes conflicting reports of Godse calling for the police versus being wrestled down by witnesses and beaten. A script should attribute both possibilities or focus on the widely reported struggle.
